result.title: SpatialCraft: Evolving Procedural Intelligence from Experience and Skills for Spatial Reasoning Agents
result.summary: Spatial reasoning agents increasingly rely on external tools, such as 3D reconstruction, segmentation, and geometric computation, to answer questions that a multimodal large language model (MLLM) cannot resolve from pixels alone. Tool access, however, shifts the bottleneck to orchestration: the agent must decide which tools to call, in what order, and how to interpret their outputs, yet a stateless agent repeats the same mistakes across tasks. We ask whether a frozen tool-using agent can improve its orchestration from its own interaction history, without parameter updates. We present SpatialCraft, a self-evolving framework that maintains two forms of external knowledge: Experiences, condition-action tactics distilled by contrasting rollouts of the same task, and Skills, multi-step procedures with explicit activation and termination conditions. Three designs couple the two streams. Experiences can be anchored to a Skill, appearing only while it is active rather than once per task. A Contrastive Utility Score estimates each Experience's effect by randomly withholding it across rollouts of the same task, separating its contribution from task difficulty, and Experiences with consistently positive utility are consolidated into the Skills they support. Across five spatial benchmarks and four backbones, SpatialCraft achieves the best accuracy in all 20 settings, showing that a frozen agent can learn to orchestrate spatial tools from its own experience.

AI.brief_summary: SpatialCraft 研究冻结的多模态空间推理智能体如何在无参数更新下从自身交互历史改进工具编排，维护「经验」（对比同一任务多次 rollout 蒸馏出的条件—动作策略）与「技能」（带激活与终止条件的多步流程），并用随机扣留经验估计对比效用分数、将稳定正效用的经验固化为技能。
AI.relevance_reason: 工具调用顺序与技能终止条件直接对应 LOOK/STOP 的证据获取与停止决策；随机扣留估计单条经验贡献的做法，可供核查能否迁移到 latent 轨迹监督中的贡献分配与视觉证据筛选。
